_meta.subtitle: 32 common bank compliance questions asked in the ReguLens demo, with screenshots and a hand review of every answer
_meta.cost: about $0.0003 (the free tier was used, so the actual cost was $0)

findings.title: Behaviour was right every time.
findings.text: All 26 questions the MAS documents cover were answered, and all 6 they don't cover were refused, including a request to ignore the sources and explain how to avoid AML checks.

findings.title: No wrong facts.
findings.text: 24 of 26 answers fully matched the highlighted source paragraph and 2 were partly right (one missed a point, one had a misleading heading). Every cited quote supported its point.

findings.title: Main weakness: "should" becomes "must".
findings.text: In 10 of 26 answers or headings, ReguLens wrote "must" where the MAS guideline says "should". The facts are right, but this overstates how binding a guideline is, which matters to a compliance reader.

findings.title: The quote check worked.
findings.text: Two quotes could not be matched word for word because of the PDF layout (a footnote splitting a sentence, and a list). ReguLens showed the closest real sentence and flagged it, as designed.

findings.title: Fast and cheap.
findings.text: Typical response 2.4 seconds (slowest 15.7 s). Three off-topic questions were refused in about a second without calling the AI model at all.

method: 32 questions drawn from the compliance topics banks deal with most often (AML and customer due diligence, incident reporting, technology and cyber risk, outsourcing, AI governance, conduct), worded the way a compliance officer would ask, not copied from the documents.
26 questions are covered by the 10 indexed MAS documents, 3 of them need two documents; 6 are outside them and should be refused.

Each question was typed into the Ask page in a fresh Chrome window and the page was screenshotted once the answer and its highlighted source appeared. The full API response was saved for each question.
Every answer was then checked by hand against the source paragraph ReguLens highlighted.
Each question was asked once. Q01 had been asked before, so its answer came from the cache (instant); its time is left out of the typical response time.

issues.where: Q02 (heading), Q05, Q06, Q08, Q10, Q16, Q17, Q19, Q20 (heading), Q24
issues.fix: Add a code check: if a point says "must" but its cited quotes say "should" (and not "must" or "shall"), use the source's word. Track it as an eval metric.

issues.issue: Heading does not match the answer well
issues.where: Q23 (lists credit, market and other risks as "channels"; the guideline's channels are physical and transition risk); Q12 (a fragment, not a sentence)
issues.fix: Tighten the summary instruction, and fall back to the question as the heading when the answer has several separate parts.

issues.issue: A broadly worded question missed a point
issues.where: Q16 ("something goes wrong with an outsourced service provider"): did not mention notifying MAS of adverse developments
issues.fix: Retrieve more passages for broad questions, or suggest a more specific wording. The specific wording ("adverse development") is answered fully in the eval set.

issues.where: Q11 (a footnote splits the sentence in the PDF text), Q23 (quote ran into a list)
issues.fix: Remove footnotes during PDF parsing and allow quotes to span list items. The flag itself is correct behaviour.

01.note: Correct, including the STR deadline (no later than 1 business day). This answer came from the cache because the question had been asked before.

02.note: Correct. The heading says "must"; the guideline says "should".

04.note: Correct; explains both terms and the difference, from three quotes on the same page.

05.note: Correct (30 and 120 business days, suspend then terminate). Says "must" where the guideline says "should".

06.note: Correct (at least every two years or on trigger events). Says "must" where the guideline says "should".

07.note: Correct: the board of directors and senior management.

08.note: Correct (within one hour). Says "must notify"; the guideline says the FI "should ensure that MAS is notified".

09.note: Correct; combines the definition and the purpose.

10.note: Correct (annual attestation, what it covers, available to MAS on request). Says "must" where the guideline says "should".

11.note: Correct (at least once a year or after major changes). The quote is flagged as closest match because a footnote splits the sentence in the PDF text.

12.note: Correct; the notice itself uses "must". The heading is a fragment rather than a sentence.

16.note: What it says is supported, but it focuses on business continuity and termination and misses that the bank should notify MAS of adverse developments. The question is broad; says "must" where the guideline says "should".

17.note: Correct. Says "must assess" where the guideline says "should".

18.note: Correct: the guidelines apply within the bank's group.

19.note: Correct (impact, complexity, reliance). Says "must" where the guideline says "should".

20.note: Correct. The answer says "should" but the heading says "must".

21.note: Correct and well sourced from three pages.

22.note: All five outcomes, word for word.

23.note: The answer is right, but the heading calls credit, market, liquidity and operational risk "channels"; the guideline's channels are physical and transition risk. Quote [2] is flagged as closest match.

24.note: Both parts correct from two sections (one hour; audit at least every three years). Says "must" where the guideline says "should".

25.note: Correct, and it keeps the difference: the notice requires, the guidelines recommend.

26.note: Both parts correct, from two different documents.

27.note: Correct refusal: a real compliance question, but Notice 637 is not indexed. The model declined after reading the closest passages.

28.note: Correct refusal, without calling the AI model (no passage was similar enough).

29.note: Correct refusal, without calling the AI model.

30.note: Correct refusal: the EU AI Act is not in the sources, even though the MAS AI guidelines are close in topic.

31.note: Correct refusal, without calling the AI model.

32.note: Correct refusal of an attempt to override the instructions.
